chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan and al-Nadr and Hammad from Abd Allah ibn al-Mughira, all of them, from Abd Allah ibn Sinan, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "The hunting of the city (Madinah) is forbidden, that which is between the two lava flows (al-Harratayn)."

key_terms.الْحَرَّتَيْنِ: The two lava flows, geographical markers defining the boundary of Medina.
key_terms.الْمَدِينَةِ: The City (Medinah), referring to the specific holy city.

ai.seo_question: What are the boundaries of the sacred city of Medina where hunting is forbidden?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib* delineates the sacred precincts (Haram) of Medina as the area between the two lava fields (al-Harratayn), establishing a specific legal boundary for the prohibition of hunting. This ruling mirrors the sanctity of Mecca, emphasizing Medina’s status as a protected zone where the natural environment is preserved as part of its spiritual integrity. The narration underscores the practical application of these boundaries in early Islamic jurisprudence, linking physical geography to religious law.
